title: A landed worktree git calls a submodule holder stays
what: Find why git sees a submodule there (a test that ran `git submodule` or wrote .git/worktrees/<name>/modules), remove the leftover, and make the landing's cleanup handle that case (or name the exact next step) instead of repeating "kept".
why: Every landing on 30 Oct (5 of 5 logs) ends with "kept .worktrees/a-land-test-leaks-gate-scripts-that-load: git refused to remove it". The branch has no commit beyond master and the tree is clean, but `git worktree remove` says "working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed", and no nested .git or gitlink is found. The leftover repeats in every land log and in relay doctor.
failing_case: 30 Oct: `git worktree remove .worktrees/a-land-test-leaks-gate-scripts-that-load` prints "fatal: working trees containing submodules cannot be moved or removed"; `find <wt> -maxdepth 5 -name .git` finds only the top .git file; `git ls-files -s` has no 160000 entry.
pass_cases: The leftover is gone and the next landing log has no "kept" line for it.
A test: a landed worktree in that state is removed by the landing, or the landing prints the one command that removes it.
